title: Console metrics flow mediator and dead-letter heuristics
creator: Marina Kovács
description: Design and implement a lightweight flow mediator layer in the realtime console metrics pipeline that smooths bursts, routes items to tenant-aware queues, and applies dead-letter heuristics for malformed or repeatedly-failing events. This ticket covers protocol-level behavior, admission control knobs exposed to Console, and the dead-letter policy (when to requeue, when to discard, and what gets surfaced to the UI and support dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: Flow mediator can detect and smooth microbursts while keeping 99th percentile tail within SLO for console ingest
Tenant-level admission controls honor configured quotas and emit metrics for token-level throttling
Dead-letter heuristics capture malformed schemas, enrichment failures after configurable retries, and unprocessable payloads into a DLQ with reason codes
Metrics and traces show end-to-end visibility (ingest -> mediator -> processor) and the Console displays DLQ counts per tenant
Feature is behind runtime feature flag and rollout can be toggled per environment
technical_design:
Introduce a flow-mediator service sitting between the edge ingest gateway and existing stream processors. Responsibilities:
- Maintain per-tenant in-memory admission window (leaky-bucket + EWMA smoothing) to avoid stampeding the downstream.
- Provide fast-path for low-latency samples (priority lanes for small chats/embeddings) and a background lane for large batchy payloads.
- Assign an idempotency token and lightweight sequence metadata for checkpoint-aware reordering downstream.
- Dead-letter decisions are rule-based: schema mismatch -> immediate DLQ; transient enrichment failures -> quick retry (2) and then DLQ with diagnostic snapshot; repeated backpressure timeouts -> requeue to deferred retry queue with exponential backoff cap.
- Expose an admission API for Console to show live tenant throttles and suggested capacity adjustments.
Implementation will reuse existing lease manager and storage checkpoints from ENG-314159 and hook into tracing from ENG-41209.
implementation_notes: Add a new K8s deployment 'console-flow-mediator' with horizontal pod autoscaler keyed to request-latency and queue-depth
Use Redis for a small, bounded per-tenant counter and EWMA state (TTL'd) to survive mediator restarts without full persistence
Serialize DLQ items to the existing dead-letter topic with a compact envelope that includes reason_code, original_offset, tenant_id, and a 1KB diagnostic sample
Provide a lightweight protobuf schema for mediator-to-processor envelope to minimize CPU overhead
Instrument p99/p999 latency, admitted_rate, dropped_rate, dlq_rate per-tenant and per-route
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flagged implementation to canary namespace (small subset of tenants). 2) Observe metrics for 48 hours: admitted_rate, dlq_rate, p99 latency. 3) Ramp to 25% tenants if stable. 4) Ramp to 100% with automated rollback threshold on dlq_rate or p99 exceeding thresholds. 5) Remove feature flag after 2 weeks of stable operation.
qa_plan: Unit tests for mediator admission logic and DLQ decision matrix; integration test simulating tenant microbursts and verifying smoothing; chaos test to restart mediator pods and ensure idempotency/duplicate-suppression; manual validation of Console DLQ UI and alerting dashboards.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Create dashboards for mediator throughput/admit/dlq by tenant and route. Add alerts:
- High DLQ rate (>0.5% of ingested events over 5m) -> P1 on-call
- p99 latency through mediator > 200ms for 10m -> P1
- Redis error rate > 1% -> P0
